heroHeadline: CRS-34 Dragon Docks at ISS (May 17, 6:37 a.m. EDT) as IFT-12 Starship Block 3 Enters T-2 Countdown — NET May 19
heroSubtitle: 8,777 days of SpaceX milestones — SpaceX Cargo Dragon C209 docked to the ISS Harmony module forward port at 6:37 a.m. EDT on May 17, 2026, arriving 28 minutes ahead of schedule and delivering 6,500 lbs of science and supplies to Expedition 74. C209 is on its sixth flight (previously CRS-22, -24, -27, -30, -32); it will remain docked for ~30 days before a Pacific splashdown in mid-June. With CRS-34 docked, SpaceX's focus shifts to Starbase: Starship IFT-12 Block 3 (Ship 39 + Booster 19, first fully Raptor-3-powered Super Heavy) is T-2 days from its NET May 19, 2026 launch window (5:30 p.m. CDT / 22:30 UTC, OLP-2). No scrub signals reported. IFT-12 will attempt to deploy 22 Starlink mass-simulator payloads and image the V3 heat shield during reentry — both stages target ocean splashdowns. SpaceX's IPO public S-1 filing window remains open (May 15–22), with the public prospectus expected as soon as the week of May 19 per CNBC; the 5-for-1 stock split (pre-split $526.59 → ~$105.32) is being processed the week of May 18. SpaceX: 58 orbital missions in 2026, 611 total booster recoveries, 10,374+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10M+ subscribers.
